def fit(d, s, kind, tx=None):
    from scipy.optimize import least_squares
    t = d['eval_times']
    dt = d['past_dt']
    (w, b) = calibrate(d)
    x = prep(s)[0] if tx is None else tx
    u = (s['past_channel_raw'] - b) @ w
    h = (s['hold_channel_raw'] - b) @ w
    y = s['strain_curves_obs'] - s['strain_0'][:, None]
    r = s['instant_rate_obs']

    def fun(p):
        (a, c) = basis(np.exp(p[:2]), dt, t, u, h, x, kind)
        return np.r_[(a @ p[2:] - y).ravel(), (c @ p[2:] - r) * 2]
    out = []
    for ts in ((0.2, 2), (0.45, 3), (0.8, 5), (0.12, 12)):
        q = least_squares(fun, np.r_[np.log(ts), np.ones(4 if kind.startswith('free') else 2), np.zeros(5)], bounds=(np.r_[np.log([0.05001] * 2), [-np.inf] * (9 if kind.startswith('free') else 7)], np.r_[np.log([24.999] * 2), [np.inf] * (9 if kind.startswith('free') else 7)]), loss='cauchy', f_scale=0.03, max_nfev=250)
        out.append(q)
    q = min(out, key=lambda q: q.cost)
    e = fun(q.x)
    return (q.x, q.cost, np.quantile(np.abs(e[:y.size]), [0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99]), np.quantile(np.abs(e[y.size:]) / 2, [0.5, 0.9, 0.99]))
